$comment: THE APP'S IDENTITY, IN ONE PLACE — criterion A10, and Owner Decision OD-2's rider.
"SmartCard / MyCard / another name remains open. Development proceeds under the working name."
"Requirement so the deferral stays free. Keep app identifier, bundle id, display name and
asset references CONFIGURABLE IN ONE PLACE from P2 onward. The existing app uses
com.smartcard.app — acceptable as a working value; DO NOT SCATTER THE STRING THROUGH SOURCE."
It was scattered: app.json held the name, slug, scheme, bundle identifier and Android package,
and three source files carried 'SmartCard' as literal text in biometric prompts and lock copy.
Renaming the product would have meant finding all of them, and the one that was missed would
have shown a user the old name at the moment they were being asked to authenticate.
WHY JSON AND NOT A .ts MODULE. Two consumers need it and they run in different worlds: Expo's
config loader evaluates app.config.js in plain Node before any TypeScript exists, and the app
imports it through the bundler. JSON is the only format both read without a build step — a .ts
source of truth would have needed a compiled copy for Expo, which is two homes again.
CHANGING A VALUE HERE IS A RENAME. app.config.js builds the Expo config from it, and
src/config/identity.ts is the app's view of the same file. Nothing else may name the product.
$storageNamespaceNote: THE STORAGE NAMESPACE IS NOT THE SLUG, AND MUST NEVER FOLLOW A RENAME.
It happens to read the same today, which is exactly why it needed separating: the A10 gate
found 'smartcard.preferences' in src/i18n/locale.ts and reported it as the slug scattered into
source. It is not. It is the id of an MMKV store that holds real users' saved preferences.
If OD-2 renames the product and this followed, every existing install would open a NEW, EMPTY
store and silently lose the user's language, their theme and their onboarding state — with no
error, because a fresh store is a valid store. A rename is a marketing decision; it must not be
So it lives here, beside the identity, marked as the one field a rename does not touch.

assets.$comment: Asset references, per OD-2's rider. Paths are relative to the repository root.
